title: Certification fields of a skills-lexicon entry (v0 draft)
$comment: Describes only the certification-related slice of an entry. Other entry fields are allowed and are checked by tools/lexicon.py. v0: to be revised after the first 25 to 50 credentials are checked against sources.

certification.description: True when the concept is a credential attested by an official body: a certification, certificate, licence, permit, endorsement or academic degree.

certification_scope.description: single-issuer: one body defines and awards it (an AWS certification, an FAA certificate). many-issuers: many independent bodies award the same kind of credential (degrees, state licences).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or INT for an international body or credential.

credential.description: Present only once the credential has been looked up. Minimum for a checked credential: a credential_type, an issuer (for a single-issuer one) and at least one source. The description is the entry's own `definition`.

official_name.description: The credential's actual name, which may differ from the entry's preferred_name.

issuers.description: Who awards it. One item for a single-issuer credential. For a many-issuers one (a degree) it may be empty until the awarding bodies are mapped, for example degree to universities.

fields.description: The field or fields of work or study the credential belongs to.

level.description: For example entry, professional, advanced, associate, bachelor, master, doctoral. Free text in v0.

specificity.description: specific-credential: one named credential. requirement-level: a level that several credentials can satisfy (DoD IAM Level I). generic-programme: a type of programme many colleges run (a certificate in welding). occupation: a job, not a credential.

status.description: Whether it can still be earned.

accreditors.description: Bodies that accredit the credential or the programmes that award it, kept apart from the issuer (CAPTE, CEPH, FSAB).

related.description: Other credentials and how they relate. Name them; link to an entry by id once one exists.

requirements.description: Exam, experience, prior degree and similar, only when a source states it.

wikipedia.description: The matching Wikipedia article. A page existing shows the credential is notable; it does not show the exact wording of the tag is a credential, and a missing page does not show it is fake.

dump.description: The dump the match was made against, for example enwiki-20261001.

verification.description: page-read: someone opened the page. search-results-only: only a search result was seen. dump-match: matched against a downloaded dump.

snippet.description: A short quote from the source. Do not copy more of Wikipedia: its text is CC BY-SA.
